questions.q: Why does this course start with Remix before moving to Foundry, per this lesson?
options: Remix is a browser-based IDE that's an easier on-ramp into writing your first real contract
Remix is what most companies actually use in production
Foundry doesn't support Solidity at all
There is no real reason — it's arbitrary
questions.explain: Remix is the easiest starting point for beginners, which is why the course begins there before moving to more advanced, industry-standard tools.

questions.q: According to the instructor's real, first-hand estimate, roughly what share of companies use Foundry vs. Hardhat?
options: About 70% Foundry, 30% Hardhat
About 30% Foundry, 70% Hardhat
50/50, exactly split
Neither is actually used by real companies
questions.explain: The instructor estimated Foundry is used about 70% of the time by companies and developers, with Hardhat making up the remaining 30%.

questions.q: What does IDE stand for, and what does one actually do?
options: Integrated Development Environment — an application for writing code, often with helpful extensions
Internet Data Exchange — a way to transfer files between computers
Independent Deployment Engine — a tool that only deploys contracts, never writes them
It has no real meaning in this context
questions.explain: An IDE (Integrated Development Environment) is an application for writing and managing code, often with extensions that assist the developer.

questions.q: No matter which tool — Remix, Foundry, or Hardhat — you use to write Solidity, what does your code ultimately compile down to and run on?
options: Bytecode, executed by the EVM
A completely different tool-specific runtime for each
Raw JavaScript
Nothing — the tools each use a different final target
questions.explain: Regardless of which development tool you use, the destination is the same: Solidity compiles to bytecode, which the EVM executes.

questions.q: Which real platform will this course primarily use going forward, per the instructor?
options: Foundry, with some Hardhat mixed in
Only Hardhat, with no exposure to Foundry
Only Remix, for the entire rest of the course
Truffle, which is actively maintained and growing
questions.explain: The instructor states the course will primarily use Foundry going forward, with some Hardhat exposure so students are prepared for either at a future job.
